page1.text:
The memory of the man who was celebrated as a hero.
The story of a knight who was not understood by anyone.

page2.text:
It is a simple story.
At the very heart of the matter, there was something wrong with him.
He had a reasonable amount of power and a fair amount of ambition.
Yet, he used his strength in the wrong places from beginning to end, and died a miserable death.

page3.text:
It came as a reasonable consequence.
Power exists to grant your own wishes.
Pity does no good for others.
There's a balance because the actions you take come back to you, or so Kirei regularly says.
One is fed because their actions circulate to generate more vitality.

page4.text:
But not having that means never being replenished.
If one lives for someone else instead of oneself, it's obvious they would run out of energy right away.
It would be like money if it were disposable.
If others use it, there is nothing left for you.
It's easy to take advantage of, and it's a given that it'll be used.
That's why in the end...
He saw many betrayals, and his life was ended by someone he saved.

page5.text:
...It just makes me mad.
I want to know why.
He worked hard, made superhuman effort even though he was an ordinary person, and he accomplished a miracle with his own blood.
His reward for that was betrayal and death. And though it seems ludicrous, he died satisfied.
It's not my place to criticize another's life.
It's not my place, but...I can't stand that one major point.

page6.text:
I've had this dream multiple times now, and that is my belief.
Usually, I wake up here.
Yet...
It seems like this morning, there's more to this dream.

page7.text: He was standing in that hell.

page8.text: It is a scene of devastation by natural means rather than human hands.

page9.text: "I would make a contract. I will serve after death, and in return, I would take compensation now."

page10.text:
He weaves a spell of contract.
Thus, he was changed as if possessed and saved those who would normally not be saved.
...Oh. This must be how he became a Heroic Spirit.

page11.text:
...From this perspective, it isn't really that great of compensation.
He probably saved a number not even in the hundreds.
This is barely qualification as a hero with such a small number, and normally it wouldn't count for the level of a Heroic Spirit.
Yet the number is irrelevant.
The qualification is one who surpasses human bounds and is able to change the fate of those destined to die.

page12.text:
Something that upends fate itself.
It doesn't matter if he is not powerful like a hero. So long as it was a disaster that could not be avoided, however small, that he changed.
No.
The world would gain a Heroic Spirit in turn, as compensation for this miracle.

page13.text:
He became a hero and saved many lives that could not have been saved.
As a result, he became a Heroic Spirit after he died and now repeats the same things he did in life.
As a servant...as a slave.
I guess the payment for the miracle is to become a disposable tool, in service of others even after death.

page14.text:
Heroic Spirits.
Superior spirits chosen by humanity. Guardian spirits of humanity.
But they are not ones with free will like Servants.
Heroic Spirits; Guardians of humanity.
Guardians do not have free will. They operate merely as sources of power.
They are extermination weapons that are only summoned to protect the world when circumstances appear that could destroy it. They are summoned to destroy these circumstances.
The Servant system is nothing more than a ritual that uses these Guardians.

page15.text:
Guardians are summoned into any era. After eliminating the threatening circumstances, they disappear.
...I would hate to be like that, but he must've been determined to take on that role.

page16.text:
In fact, he might've even desired it.
Nothing made him happier than being able to save people even after he died.
Since he didn't have the power to save them when he was alive, he must've believed that he could avert any tragedy once he became a Heroic Spirit.
With that in mind, he readily made a deal with the world to give up his life after death, and saved a hundred lives.
...After that...
He believed that he could save tens of thousands more.

page17.text:
What an idiot.
There's no way that could be possible.
Because by the time a Heroic Spirit is summoned, where they appear has already gone to hell.
Places where Heroic Spirits—Guardians—appear are only hell.
They only appear when the world is about to be destroyed by mankind.
Humans are creatures that perish from their own doings.
That's why the process of destruction is always the same.

page18.text:
Jealousy. Hatred. Selfishness. Desire.
The man who loved and tried to be of help to others was shown the same ugliness even after he died.
He is summoned to such places and fulfills his responsibilities, just as the contract says.

page19.text:
He killed.
He killed and killed and killed and killed. He killed all the humans where he was summoned to save humanity as a whole.
I don't know how many times he repeated it... Nor do I have the means to know how many more times he will continue to repeat it.

page20.text:
...There's only one thing I can say.
He has been betrayed by many things...
But in the end, he was betrayed by the only thing he believed in: his ideals.

page21.text:
"Geez..."
When I wake up, I have nothing useful to say.
My body feels strangely tired and I can't move from the bed.
My mind is the only thing that's clear, and still I blankly stare at the ceiling.

page22.text:
"...I had a feeling. That was his memory after all."
I sigh and gaze at the ceiling.
...This sucks.
He could've told me that I might get a glimpse of his memories while I'm sleeping since Masters and Servants are connected spiritually.
If he told me, I could've cut my consciousness so I wouldn't have to deal with that.

page23.text:
"...I should get up. I have a lot to do today."
I get my body out of bed.
My body feels heavy, and my eyelids are as heavy as stone.
I resent how I'm not a morning person and slowly change from my pajamas to my uniform.

page24.text:
"But, well..."
I'm not sure whether it makes sense or it was unexpected.
He used to be a pretty hot-blooded man back in the day.
I don't know what hero he was, but he seemed more honest in the past.

page25.text:
"...Well, I guess it's natural for his personality to get twisted after living a life like that and yet having to be in such a situation even after death."
I have a brief laugh.
My reflection in the mirror looks so serious like I'm about to cry, so I try to laugh it off.
Otherwise I won't be able to face Archer at all.

page26.text:
I get ready and drink the freshly brewed tea in the living room.
I don't usually eat breakfast, so I'm quick.
There's fifteen minutes until I have to leave for school. This cup of tea is like a ritual I perform every morning to wake my half-asleep body.
"Rin, how long are you going to be playing around for?"
Yet, there's one fool that can't read the room.

page27.text:
"Until 7:30. I'll be late if I stay longer than that."
"I'm not asking about when you have to leave for school. I'm asking about the Holy Grail War.
...It's not a bad thing to pair with other Masters. But the partner you chose is too weak."
"...Ugh."
That again?
Archer keeps on suggesting that I cut off my truce with Shirou Emiya at every chance he gets.

page28.text:
"I told you I have no intention of doing so. You say that, but I think he's fit for it. It's true he's not much help in battle, but he's perfect as an ally.
...Because, well, I think he would never betray me no matter what."

page29.text:
"Trust is a point of negotiation. I cannot trust someone without a reason in return. Look, that is not someone who can survive and win. If you are to choose an ally, Caster's Master is more clever."
"Don't be ridiculous, Archer. You're telling me to stoop so low to match their devilishness?"
I set my teacup down and look at Archer.
Even if it was sarcasm, I can't ignore his implication.

page30.text:
...
...
...The atmosphere freezes.
I'm seriously getting pissed, and Archer looks like he has no intention of backing down.
We stare each other down.

page31.text:
"It's true that Caster is a schemer, but she is indeed like a mage.
In that regard, you are not suited for battle. If you're a mage, you should prioritize results over ambitions."
"Your cynicism won't get you anywhere. I won't change my policy."
"...The hell is your problem, anyway? You've been acting strange ever since you met Shirou Emiya. Where did that rationality of yours go?"

page32.text:
...
...Hmph.
I realize that without you even having to say it.
But I can't help it.
He hasn't gained anything even though he's a mage, and he's dangerously narrow-minded.
There's no use in trying to scheme against such a guy, and besides...he's, um...

page33.text:
"Rin? What happened? Finally get a bead on your own stupidity?"
"...Yes. I suppose there's something wrong with me.
But Archer. This is all your fault for letting me know things."
"What?"

page34.text: "...Never mind, forget it. Anyway, you're my Servant, got that? I'm only going to do what I believe is right. I'm not as naïve as Emiya, but I do have things I won't give up on. No matter who is telling me to."

page35.text:
I can't clamp down on the anger.
And that makes me realize...
I don't feel any sympathy, even after learning about his past.
I'm just mad.

page36.text:
"...Hmph. I can't hear you, Archer!?"
So I take it out on him as much as I can.
The knight in the red coat sighs and assumes what seems to be his favorite pose.
"Nothing I can do about it, I guess. It is the role of a retainer to support a master, well or not. I shall look after you from the sidelines until you are back to your usual self."
And he replies with an answer that's neither yes or no.
